subject.title: [Bug]: Browser interactions can exhaust model context by injecting too much page content

question: Should the browser tool make compact goal-shaped reads and small post-action change signals the default interaction contract, or keep the current capped snapshot behavior with opt-in efficient mode?
rationale: The remaining work changes model-facing browser semantics and compatibility with full snapshot workflows, so automation should not choose the default contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt Compact Browser Defaults
options.body: Make compact, goal-shaped reads and small post-action change signals the default while preserving explicit raw/full snapshot access.

options.title: Keep Current Capped Behavior
options.body: Retain 40,000-character AI snapshots and opt-in efficient mode, treating further compaction as targeted future work.

options.title: Defer To Broader Context Work
options.body: Track browser output pressure under the broader context/tool-output compression architecture instead of changing browser defaults now.

recommendation.title: Adopt Compact Browser Defaults
recommendation.body: Make compact, goal-shaped reads and small post-action change signals the default while preserving explicit raw/full snapshot access.

likelyOwner.reason: The browser snapshot default mode and current browser plugin semantics history make this the strongest routing candidate for the product-contract choice.
